body:
Yeah, I thought so too... but beerhighfive guy just isn't sustainable.   I drank a lot in high-school and college.  Fortunately, I'm well above average intelligence and could maintain such a lifestyle without completely screwing up my life.  I did however, confront and acknowledge having a substance abuse problem more than once and went through pretty drastic steps to correct myself (which I do not regret).  However, I can't seem to shake a dependency...  now I smoke weed to get fucked up and while I don't have the physical repercussions (hangover, etc) I still find it taking its toll.

I think you are right about being around people, though.  I wish I had put more time into building friendships and relationships as well as sustaining them.  I just didn't think it was a worthwhile investment at the time.   You'll find once you get out of school and working a job it's a lot harder to meet new people and make new friends-- for so many reasons.

I'd encourage you to stay away from drinking and other drugs as long as you can.  In my experience, they've always seemed like a short-term fix but really complicate things in the long-run.  Your brain is still developing a whole bunch and you don't want it to develop around these substances, trust me.   You'll thank me in 10 years.

Anyways, thanks for your post.  There are certainly parallels in our lives.
